Antoni, M., Rossen, J., Martirena, F. and Scrivener, K. (2012). Cement substitution by a combination of metakaolin and limestone. Cement and Concrete Research, 42(12), 1579-1589. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cemconres.2012.09.006

NO TECHNOLOGY PARAMETERS EXTRACTED. Laboratory materials-science study (mortars and pastes; XRD, TGA, MIP, calorimetry, thermodynamic modelling) of coupled metakaolin:limestone (2:1) substitution of Portland cement at 15, 30, 45 and 60%. No energy use, cost, capacity or emissions. Its technology-relevant findings: 45% substitution (30% metakaolin + 15% limestone, i.e. 55% Portland cement) gives better 7- and 28-day strength than 100% PC; 60% substitution reaches 93% of PC strength at 28 days; kaolinitic clays are calcined at 600-800 degC to metakaolin (intro, p.1579); above ~30% substitution conventional SCMs reduce early strength; gypsum must be balanced (1.5% addition optimal). These composition facts are superseded at technology level by scrivener_2018_001 (LC3-50: 50% clinker, 30% calcined clay, 15% limestone, 5% gypsum).
